answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity costly: to join, an agent locks a refundable deposit, like a falcon tethered to its perch, and the bond is slashed if the identity misbehaves. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake inlet separately, so forging a thousand agents costs a thousand deposits, while honest agents pay once and earn the jade of reputation over time. The deposit turns cheap duplication into an expensive, auditable commitment.
